verdict.reasoning: Patient states chest tightness for about three hours: 'my chest has been feeling really tight.' and 'for about. Three hours now.'
Patient reports mild shortness of breath and wheeze: 'Yeah, like a little bit, um. Yeah, a little bit short of breath, not too bad.' and 'Yeah, I'm feeling a bit wheezy, as well.'
Doctor summarizes 'it's non-productive cough,' and patient has not been coughing anything up: 'And are you coughing up anything? Patient: Uh, no.'
Patient describes recent cold symptoms consistent with URTI: 'You know I had a cold last week... I had a sore throat, I had a runny nose. Uh, just feeling under the weather.'
Patient notes improvement in runny nose and sore throat: 'it's not as bad as it was' and 'the runny nose isn't as bad any more.'

Patient says cough is 'pretty consistent' with only slight worsening at night: 'it gets a little bit worse at night but, basically, just pretty consistent, and it hasn't gone away.' The fact states it is worse at night, overstating severity.

Patient is not short of breath at rest but is on stairs: 'I'm definitely not short of breath at rest' and 'when I'm walking up stairs, I do feel like, I have a little bit, more short of breath than I would normally be.'

Patient expresses anxiety about a severe attack/intubation: 'It's just kinda scary, 'cause I haven't had, a time like this where I've been so, tight, uh, in a long time.' and 'I just don't wanna have to get, um, that, that intubation again.'

Patient mentions childhood eczema: 'ohh, when I was young, I also had eczema.'
Patient had a milk protein allergy: 'And I had a milk protein allergy, when I was young too.'

Patient used Salbutamol (Ventolin) and ran out about a week ago: 'you know the um, uh, Ventolin. It's called uh, Salbutamol... I forgot to bring it with me, so I haven't really in the past week... they ran out and I, I forgot to, go and grab the next one. ... About a week ago.'

Same applies to Clenil Modulite inhaler: 'and then I have a steroid, a Clenil, Clenil inhaler.' and 'I forgot to bring it with me, so I haven't really in the past week... they ran out... About a week ago.' and doctor confirms 'you haven't got any Clenil, or any Ventolin at the moment?'
Patient denies drug allergies: 'any drug allergies, that you know of? Patient: No, no, not allergic to anything. Just like, just the, dust and stuff, but nothing, no drugs.'
Patient reports dust allergy: 'And then I have like, a hayfever, you know, and some allergies just to dust, stuff like that.'
Patient’s mother has eczema: 'my mum has eczema.'
Patient’s father has asthma: 'and my dad has asthma.'
Patient mentions being away at university last week: 'I was away at uni last week, and I forgot to bring it with me.' This implies current university student.

Clinically consistent and implied: recent viral URTI ('I had a cold last week'), lapse in both controller and reliever for about a week ('I forgot to bring it... they ran out'), and current wheeze, cough, chest tightness labeled by doctor as 'this asthma attack.'
While hay fever is mentioned ('I have like, a hayfever'), there is no statement that it is currently 'stable' or about its current activity level.

Doctor plans Ventolin with spacer: 'get you some, uh, Ventolin, Clenil Modulite.' and 'the other thing I'd like to send you is a spacer, which would allow the medication to actually, go into your lungs better.' and instructs Ventolin as PRN: 'Ventolin as a PRN... when you need to.'

Doctor plans ongoing Clenil maintenance: 'send you these, the, some prescriptions for your, uh, inhalers, , ongoing... you can... use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN.' This is consistent with BID-type maintenance though exact BID wording isn't used.

Doctor prescribes a 5‑day oral steroid course, 2 tablets in the morning: 'give you a, dose of steroids. So this is, these are tablets which, um, you can take for five days. Uh, two tablets in the morning.' Prednisolone is the standard implied agent.

Doctor provides spacer technique education and red-flag advice; asthma action is implicitly covered: 'it has some instructions about how to use it, but essentially, uh, couple of puffs to prime it, inside, breathing in and out, um, uh, for five or , five or ten breaths.' and 'If you should start to use the Ventolin more than, uh, every three hours... seek medical attention.' and 'Any deterioration in your symptoms... then, seek further medical attention anytime please.'

Doctor advises rest and mentions self-certifying sick leave up to 7 days: 'I might give you some time off work as well. You can self-certify first seven days, but uh, I think I would advise you just to, rest a little bit until you're feeling a bit better.'

Doctor advises seeking care if condition worsens: 'If you should start to use the Ventolin more than, uh, every three hours... seek medical attention.' and 'Any deterioration in your symptoms... then, seek further medical attention anytime please.'
